newsitem.title: USA: US Senate Energy panel holds electricity workshops.
newsitem.headline: US Senate Energy panel holds electricity workshops.

text.p: In an effort to get a freer discussion on the complex issue, the U.S. Senate Energy Committee will hold three workshops instead of formal hearings next month on electricity deregulation, committee staff said Tuesday.
The workshops are to be held March 4, 11 and 18, the staff said in a briefing.
The workshops are to be on the issue of competitiveness, the role of public power in a competitive market and on whether federal legislation is necessary.

To get "a more freeflowing discussion of the issues," committee staff said Chairman Frank Murkowski, an Alaska Republican, wanted workshops instead of hearings in which a series of witnesses give presentations and senators have a limited time for questions.
The staff said formal legislative hearings may be held later, if necessary.
The committee held four formal hearings on the issue last year.

The staff also said Murkowski at this time does not plan to introduce his own electricity deregulation bill, but may introduce a "chairman's mark" once the process of working through various bills has reached that stage.
"We'll wait until we've got some ripe pieces of legislation," one staffer said.
Ranking committee Democrat Dale Bumpers of Arkansas has offered his own deregulation legislation.
